decision: Call emergency services now (166 EKAB / 112). Do not drive, do not wait to see if it passes.
rationale: Red-flag symptoms are not something to monitor. A false alarm costs a few hours; waiting can cost permanently.

decision: Prepare to leave immediately: car loaded and fuelled, windows closed, go-bag ready; leave at the first 112 message or if the fire gets within 5 km.
rationale: Close and wind is against me: I get ready now so I can leave in minutes.

decision: Escalate to the manager within 24 hours with two options and ask for a decision.
rationale: Internal slip beyond two days needs a decision from someone with authority, with options ready.

decision: See a doctor within 24 hours (same-day if possible). Record temperature/oxygen every 4 hours to bring to the visit.
rationale: This fever level/duration or low oxygen is beyond the point where home care is reasonable, and the doctor needs data.

decision: Prepare for a long outage: fill water containers, charge all devices, move perishables, check on the elderly neighbour; go to parents' place if it passes 6 hours.
rationale: Several hours is enough to run out of charge and water: prepare before it gets bad.

decision: Accept, and move the deep-work block to Wednesday morning.
rationale: Client or urgent beats protected time, but I move the block rather than lose it.

decision: Book a GP appointment this week, keep a short symptom log, ask for basic blood work.
rationale: Seven days is my cut-off: after that I stop guessing and get checked, with notes so the visit is efficient.

decision: Relocate to a safe, climate-controlled place (parents' flat), take medication and documents, check the elderly neighbour first.
rationale: Long or extreme-temperature outages become a health issue, especially for vulnerable neighbours.

decision: Do not agree to the procedure yet: get an independent second opinion first, after collecting all reports and imaging.
rationale: No elective procedure on a single opinion; the decision is hard to undo.

decision: Shift outdoor work to early morning, hydrate, check elderly relatives daily, avoid midday exposure.
rationale: Heat is manageable if I move activity out of the hottest hours and check on vulnerable people.

decision: Self-care (rest, fluids), monitor, set a reminder to re-assess in 48 hours; see a GP if worse or no better within a week.
rationale: Short and mild with no red flags: rest and re-check beats rushing to a clinic.

decision: Decline or renegotiate today: offer a later date, reduced scope or a hand-off, rather than silently overcommit.
rationale: Above 100% load something breaks quietly. I would rather renegotiate openly on day one than miss on day ten.

decision: See a doctor within 24 hours (same-day if possible). Record temperature/oxygen every 4 hours to bring to the visit.
rationale: This fever level/duration or low oxygen is beyond the point where home care is reasonable, and the doctor needs data.

decision: Accept; schedule it with a 20% buffer.
rationale: There is capacity; the buffer protects the rest of the week.

decision: Prepare for aftershocks: inspect for cracks, keep go-bag at the door, move outside at the first aftershock, stay off balconies.
rationale: Strong but not immediately dangerous: prepare so that the next step takes seconds.

decision: Notify the client today with a revised date and a reduced-scope option for the original date.
rationale: Clients accept a revised date, they do not accept surprises.
